plain_description.what: Pools two repeated runs of the same judge (grok) on identical inputs to test whether a calibration parameter of the judge's error model can be estimated reliably. The pooled data holds 46 cases where the board ordered a model pair in the wrong direction, which are only 29 distinct pairs. It also sets rules for when a re-judge is needed. No calls.
plain_description.why: One run met the bar and the other did not; pooling asks whether the judge's error calibration is actually identified, which underpins trusting ordered per-cell judged rankings.
plain_description.information: Identification would support ordered judged rankings for this judge; failure would downgrade them. Result: done. It passes the registered bar, but the two runs share most of the same errors (the 46 wrong orderings are only 29 distinct model pairs). Once that overlap is accounted for, it is not significant at the usual 5% level (p about 0.07). No cell is downgraded. Older p2dca question family, later ruled 'history, not evidence'.
